Water from your late-evening shower still drips from the ends of your hair onto your collarbone. Outside the frosted naco louver blades, monsoon rain hammers the Amano tin roof. Your washed clothes are still hanging on the concrete balcony wire. The wall clock reads

paragraphs.text: By nine o'clock the rain settles into a relentless, suffocating drumbeat on the tin roof. Fatigue pulls at your eyelids, heavy and warm, though the air in the corner of the room has turned bitingly cold.

Directly opposite the foot of your bed stands the tall wooden dressing table. Its unshrouded mirror faces your pillow. In the dim amber glow of the brass wick, the tarnished glass reflects the white mosquito net hanging over your mattress—and

paragraphs.wakingText: the empty shadow of the wardrobe behind it
paragraphs.corruptedText: a dark, broad-shouldered silhouette standing just behind the net

paragraphs.text: You lean toward the glass. Your own eyes stare back, wide and dark, framed by damp strands of hair. For three heartbeats nothing moves.

A message banner glows on the dark glass:

paragraphs.wakingText: Amma: Did you lock the balcony door properly?
paragraphs.corruptedText: He is already inside the net with you. Let go of the iron key.

paragraphs.text: The mattress sinks beside your hip. A crushing, velvet weight settles directly across your sternum, pinning your ribs until your lungs burn for air.

Seven overlapping voices whisper from the corners of the ceiling like rustling silk sarees, while a face of polished night leans down through the mesh. His breath smells of sandalwood paste, frying oil, and river silt. He whispers into your ear:

paragraphs.wakingText: Open your fingers. Drop the cold iron and sleep.

paragraphs.text: The iron key bites deep into your palm, warm with your pulse. As the first crow calls from the wet jak tree outside and a morning bus horn echoes down High Level Road, the crushing weight lifts from your chest all at once.

The brass pahana flame snaps upright, burning clear golden-amber again. On the floor outside the mosquito net lies a single bruised Nil Manel petal, already shriveling into harmless black ash in the grey dawn light. You survived the Samayam watch unbroken.

Three days later, the private hospital in Colombo discharges you with unexplained delirium and a fever that will not break. You lie staring at the ceiling fan, whispering to the empty corner by the mirror, while your terrified mother sends a Bulath Hurulla sheaf south to summon a Kattadiya.

paragraphs.text: It is 10:15 PM on Friday. You sit cross-legged on a woven reed mat in the narrow living room of the Nugegoda annex, your brass pahana burning steadily before you. In the bedroom behind the curtain, the twenty-one-year-old student murmurs feverishly in her sleep.

Her mother kneels and places the Bulath Hurulla sheaf into your hands. Following the silent discipline of the Sastra-kariya, you ask zero questions. You lift the top dark-green betel leaf toward the golden flame to read the Lakunu encoded in its veins.

choices.label: Pass the Pahana flame behind the betel leaf to read its veins and blemishes

paragraphs.text: As the amber light pierces the waxy blade of the betel leaf, the internal geometry glows like gold wire. The stem bends northwest toward the canal.

Where dusk water touched her hair, a dark bruise clouds the leaf apex; where the unshrouded mirror caught her reflection, a pinhole pierces the midrib; where sweet oil-cakes or damp laundry lingered past six o'clock, oily knots thicken the lower veins. This is not natural fever:

paragraphs.wakingText: the veins appear calm at first glance

paragraphs.text: Inside the cramped bedroom, you press three fingers to the girl's wrist. Her Nadi pulse leaps erratically between Vatha and Pitta—hot blood racing beneath ice-cold skin.

You inspect the room without speaking: the vanity mirror stands directly aligned with the pillow, the balcony louver latch smells faintly of bruised water-lilies, and ants trail toward an old tin of sweetmeats. There is no buried Kodivina charm beneath the threshold; she was struck in Tanikama during the dusk watch.

paragraphs.text: Midnight approaches. In the tight annex living room, you lash split bamboo and pale yellow gokkola strips into a square Pideni Thattuwa frame. At the four cardinal points you set seven bruised flowers, sweet kevum, charred pulutu meat, and powdered dummala resin.

In the center rests the wet clay Bali Pili effigy of the Dark Prince. Before sealing the offering with blood and turmeric, you must turn the effigy's face toward the exact avatar revealed by the betel leaf: East toward the sweetmeats for the seductive Handun Kumara, or West toward the burnt offerings for the suffocating Vatha Kumara.

choices.label: Turn the clay effigy East to bind Handun Kumara and begin the Samayama

paragraphs.text: The low-country yak bera drum thunders against the apartment walls. You cast a handful of dummala resin across the torch flame—a sheet of blinding amber fire roars toward the ceiling, forcing the shadow out of the bedroom doorway.
The pahana flame bends flat, turning indigo as Kalu Kumara tries to twist your tongue inside the mantra:

paragraphs.wakingText: You have no jurisdiction in a concrete city, old man
paragraphs.corruptedText: By the Varama of the Buddha and the Seven Barren Queens, confess and depart

paragraphs.text: With the iron ward locked under your thumb, your voice cuts through the indigo smoke without faltering. You bring the plantain blade down across the edge of the Pideni Thattuwa. A sharp crack echoes through the room as the clay effigy splits cleanly down its chest, accepting the surrogate tribute.

In the bedroom, the girl draws a long, clear breath. Her fever breaks into cool sweat. You knot the white Pirith Nula thread three times around her wrist as the first light of dawn touches the Nugegoda rooftops, carrying the woven tray out to the crossroads to rot in the sun.

paragraphs.text: The last bus down to the Kandy clock tower left twenty minutes ago. Cold mist rolls off the black surface of the lake below, swallowing the curve of Upper Lake Road in a wet, chalky shroud.

To your left, the moss-slick stone retaining wall borders the giant bamboo thickets of Udawattakele Sanctuary. It is 11:46 PM. Around your right wrist, the white three-knotted Pirith Nula thread from the Dalada Maligawa feels damp against your pulse. Up ahead, the single municipal streetlamp flickers with

paragraphs.text: In the courtyard beneath a temporary gokkola canopy, the yak bera drum begins its rolling cadence. Before the altar stand three carved Ambalangoda masks of Kaduru wood alongside a freshly cut green banana stem—the Kesel Kanda—wrapped in white cloth like an infant.

You dance the first two states in sequence: first the blandly alluring pink Coquette mask to draw the patient's gaze toward the arena; then the grotesquely swollen Pregnancy mask, groaning under a crushing burden until the boy shudders in revulsion. Now comes the final severance.

You dip a fresh three-stranded Pirith Nula into turmeric water, chant the protective gatha, and knot it tightly around his right wrist as the mist over the Kandy hills turns pale gold with dawn.

paragraphs.text: A bruisingslash of crimson light—the Lē Irabatuwa sunset—bleeds through the clay smoke-tiles of your grandmother's outdoor firewood kitchen in Matara. The main house stands thirty yards away across the wet laterite courtyard.

In the heavy iron pan over the dara lipa hearth, coconut oil hisses around pieces of salted seer fish. As you turn a fillet with the iron ladle, the sharp fin nicks the ball of your thumb. A single bead of blood swells against your skin, and the rising steam smells suddenly of

paragraphs.corruptedText: scorched copper and raw slaughterhouse iron

Outside the low wooden doorway, something heavy scrapes across the gravel by the chopping block. In the red twilight, the puddle of fish-cleaning water you poured beside the threshold glints like

paragraphs.text: Darkness drops fast over the southern coast. Along the boundary wall separating the garden from the old canal lane, the row of Wada Mal bushes hangs heavy with wet, blood-red hibiscus blossoms.

From the hollow vents of the clay mound comes a low, rasping hiss, followed by the unmistakable stench of

paragraphs.text: By midnight, a sudden, violent heat surges behind your eyes. You sink onto the woven reed mat in the corner of the kitchen as your pulse hammers against your eardrums like a double-headed drum.

Through the smoke-vent grating near the roof tiles, two small, bloodshot eyes peer down through the soot. The voice that scrapes from the rafters is not human; it chatters with the wet, feral cadence of a macaque:

paragraphs.wakingText: The rain is leaking through the old clay tiles

A squat, muscular figure smeared in vermilion lime crouches on the threshold stone, holding a torn red hibiscus blossom between its teeth. Every heartbeat in your chest feels as if

The heat in your veins turns to freezing lead. In the roaring silence of your ears, the demon demands its warrant:

At daybreak, your family finds you stretched motionless on the kitchen reed mat, your skin burning with a dry scarlet fever while your lips murmur toward the termite mound. An urgent Bulath Hurulla sheaf is dispatched to a Matara Yakadura master.

The household elder places the Bulath Hurulla sheaf beside your brass lamp. Observing the strict silence of the Southern Sastra tradition, you hold the top betel leaf before the flame.

paragraphs.text: You examine the patient's tongue and wrists: the Pitta and Rakta humours are boiling. Out by the kitchen well, crushed red Wada Mal petals lie pressed into the mud beside the termite mound, and the iron frying pan still reeks of dusk pulutu.
Whether struck by the frenzied Maru Riri or the corpse-cold Sohon Riri, the demon will not depart until he witnesses a body wrapped and bound for the cremation ground.

choices.label: Spread the woven rush mat in the courtyard for the Dara Haeva ritual

paragraphs.text: In the sandy courtyard between the kitchen and the well, flares of dummala resin turn the drizzle blood-red. You spread a fresh Pan Pedura rush mat upon the earth and mix turmeric with slaked lime until the water turns deep arterial crimson—Rathu Kaha Diya.

To satisfy Riri Yaka's demand for a corpse, you must anoint the three vital chakras on the mat with crimson lime-water, fold the woven rush shroud over the surrogate form, and knot the three gokkola funeral bindings at the head, heart, and feet.

choices.label: Seal the three gokkola funeral knots and chant the Riri Yak Varama

paragraphs.text: The Southern yak bera drum hammers a funeral march. As the bound rush mat lies between the flaming torches, a squat shadow drops from the hibiscus hedge, sniffing the crimson turmeric-lime water spilled across the reeds.
The lamp flame flattens as Riri Yaka reaches for the living patient on the verandah instead of the mat:

paragraphs.wakingText: The boy on the cot still has warm blood in his throat
paragraphs.corruptedText: Accept this bound corpse on the funeral mat and depart to the charnel ground

paragraphs.text: . You must lock the iron ward and strike the final gatha cadence to transfer the warrant into the mat.

choices.label: Hold the iron ward, recite the Riri Yak Varama, and cast the mat beyond the gate
Cut the gokkola funeral ties without anchoring the iron ward

paragraphs.text: With the iron ward locked under your thumb, you slice the تین gokkola knots with a single downward stroke and hurl the red lime-water into the darkness beyond the boundary wall. Deceived by the funeral shroud and sated by the crimson tribute, the shadow vanishes into the canal mist.
On the verandah, the scarlet flush fades from the patient's cheeks. He sits up and asks for cool water as the morning sun clears the Matara palms.

paragraphs.text: Your thumb slips from the iron ward before the funeral transfer is sealed. The middle gokkola tie snaps prematurely, and the woven rush mat unrolls empty in the mud.

A chattering laugh echoes from the kitchen roof tiles as the brass lamp tips over in a pool of red lime-water. You must re-anoint the rush mat and bind the funeral shroud anew before the patient's pulse gives out.

choices.label: Spread the Pan Pedura mat again and repeat the funeral binding

paragraphs.text: The dynamo headlamp on your bicycle flickers and dies as the chain slips off the sprocket. You come to a halt at the Thummansala—the deserted three-way gravel junction where the Anuradhapura tank-bund track meets the old village cremation ground.

It is 11:52 PM. Overhead, the aerial roots of an ancient banyan tree hang motionless in the dry, moonless air. Somewhere in the thorny scrub, a nightjar clicks once, and the silence presses against your eardrums like

paragraphs.wakingText: warm dry-zone wind
paragraphs.corruptedText: a giant holding its breath six paces behind your back

choices.label: Whistle a loud tune to steady your nerves while fitting the greasy bicycle chain
Work in strict silence and keep one thumb on the iron Giraya cutter in your pocket

paragraphs.text: Your whistle dies flat against the banyan trunks—no echo returns from the tank water. Hanging from your handlebar is a newspaper-wrapped parcel of spiced wild boar curry from your uncle's almsgiving house.
The paper has soaked through with warm fat. As you crouch over the rear wheel, a sudden gust of wind carrying the stench of

paragraphs.wakingText: dry palu leaves and tank mud
paragraphs.corruptedText: wet grave-earth and scorched boar bristles

paragraphs.text: sweeps across the junction.

choices.label: Leave the meat parcel uncovered in the basket without tucking an iron nail inside
Slip your forged iron betel-cutter into the meat wrapper to seal the scent

paragraphs.text: You hook the chain back onto the teeth without making a sound, though your fingers come away black with axle grease. Tied to your carrier rack is a warm parcel of roasted meat from the village feast.
Down inside the dry concrete culvert beneath the crossroads, dry leaves rustle violently—as if something far too broad to fit inside a pipe is

paragraphs.wakingText: a monitor lizard burrowing in the silt
paragraphs.corruptedText: dragging a crushed shoulder along the concrete wall

choices.label: Pedal away fast without warding the meat parcel on your carrier
Press the iron Giraya against the parcel and walk the bicycle past the culvert

paragraphs.text: Right at the center of the three-way fork lies a shattered red-clay muttiya pot from a previous night's exorcism. White wood-ash, charred chicken bones, and tarnished copper coins form a pale barrier across the tire ruts.
Beyond the pot, the gravel rises toward the Wewa tank bund. In the dim starlight, the spilled white ash on the road shifts into the shape of

paragraphs.wakingText: windblown lime dust
paragraphs.corruptedText: a giant five-fingered handprint pointing toward the cemetery

choices.label: Kick the broken clay shards aside and roll straight through the ritual ash
Steer wide into the thorny grass to avoid touching the crossroads ash
Hold the cold iron Giraya and trace a protective line in the gravel

paragraphs.text: You push the bicycle up the steep earthen slope of the tank bund. To your left, black water laps against the sluice stones; to your right, the rusted barbed-wire fence of the village Susāna Bhūmiya cemetery leans into the tall grass.

Five yards behind your rear fender, a dead palu branch as thick as a man's thigh snaps with a sound like a rifle shot. Heavy, uneven footsteps—one stride long, the next dragging—thud across the gravel, and a guttural grunt breathes down your neck:

paragraphs.wakingText: It is only a stray water buffalo on the bund
paragraphs.corruptedText: Turn around and see whose head rests backwards on my shoulders

choices.label: Whip your head around to see what is following you on the bund
Keep your eyes locked straight ahead on the bund path and grip the iron Giraya

paragraphs.text: The wild boar's tusked snout rears twelve cubits tall into the weeping banyan roots. Steam billows from flared nostrils, smelling of charred marrow and crushed areca husk. Its blood-red eyes reflect the distant temple lights, and a low, mocking chortle grates from its backwards-turned throat:

paragraphs.wakingText: A herd animal rooting in the tank mud
paragraphs.corruptedText: Jayasena remembers the kick of Gothaimbara across your shoulder

choices.label: Pedal frantically through the gravel toward the boundary pillar
Stand your ground, gripping the forged iron Giraya in your fist

paragraphs.text: At the end of the cemetery fence stands the whitewashed boundary pillar. Perched atop the four-foot stone—yet rising twelve feet into the branches—crouches a colossal figure smeared in cremation ash, its left shoulder caved inward from Gothaimbara's ancient kick, topped by the bristling, tusked head of a wild boar.
In its right fist it crushes a human-shaped gourd, drinking the pale sap. The air reeks of dummala smoke and wet fur as

paragraphs.wakingText: the wind shakes the banyan canopy
paragraphs.corruptedText: the giant raises an open five-fingered palm above your spine

choices.label: Shout a curse and swing your bicycle pump at the boar-headed shadow
Bow your chin, clamp your thumb on the iron Giraya, and step backward without turning

paragraphs.text: A sudden, sickening shockwave—the Gassīma—ripples up your spine, unseating your balance on the pedals. The horizon tilts forty-five degrees to the west, and the sound of the crickets vanishes into total vacuum. Behind your left shoulder blade, the air turns to freezing grease:

paragraphs.wakingText: Your balance failed on the steep tank incline
paragraphs.corruptedText: The cemetery king prepares his five-fingered seal

choices.label: Throw your arms out as the cold pressure locks your vertebrae
Press the cold-iron arecanut cutter into your chest and recite the protective formula

paragraphs.text: The sky above the tank bund seems to drop like a granite slab. Before you can draw another breath, a freezing, concussive blow slams squarely between your shoulder blades—not like a fist, but like a sack of wet grave-ash dropped from the treetops.
You pitch forward onto your knees in the gravel. Your spine locks rigid, your teeth chatter uncontrollably, and the towering shadow looms over the bicycle frame:

paragraphs.wakingText: You merely slipped on the loose tank gravel
paragraphs.corruptedText: My five fingers are branded in black soot across your back

choices.label: Press the forged iron Giraya against your breastbone and spit three times onto the earth
Collapse across the bicycle frame as the freezing tremor paralyzes your lungs
Turn on your back to stare up at the boar-headed titan in the dark

paragraphs.text: The cold iron Giraya bites into your palm, anchoring your spirit against the shockwave. A furious, boar-like snort tears through the banyan leaves, showering the road with dry twigs, before receding into the cemetery mist as the temple bell rings for the dawn watch.
When you stagger home at daybreak, your cotton shirt is scorched at the left shoulder, but the skin beneath is whole.

paragraphs.text: The shockwave extinguishes your sight. When woodcutters find you beside the three-way culvert at dawn, you are curled in the red gravel, shivering with a violent ague.

When your elders peel back your torn shirt, a stark, five-fingered handprint of greasy black soot is stamped deep into the skin over your left shoulder blade. A runner is sent immediately with a Bulath Hurulla sheaf to summon a master of the Mahasona Samayama.

choices.label: Accept the Bulath Hurulla and step into the Kattadiya role

paragraphs.text: You arrive at the patient's compound in Anuradhapura as the bamboo Vidiya altar is erected in the sandy courtyard. Inside the house, the patient shakes with bone-rattling chills, unable to turn his stiffened neck to the left.
The household head offers the Bulath Hurulla sheaf beside your brass lamp. Before donning the boar-tusked mask, you raise the top betel leaf against the Pahana flame to read the crossroads signature.

choices.label: Hold the Pahana behind the betel leaf to inspect the five crossroads Lakunu
Inspect the black five-fingered handprint on the patient's shoulder first

paragraphs.text: Through the translucent leaf blade, the charnel marks stand out starkly: a dark bruise at the tip from midnight whistling at the Thummansala, a knotted left vein from unwarded meat, and a central tear where the victim looked back on the tank bund.
The diagnosis is certain:

paragraphs.wakingText: the chill is merely malaria from the tank reeds
paragraphs.corruptedText: Mahasona has struck the spine at the three-way boundary

paragraphs.text: . Fear only feeds the Great Cemetery Demon—to shrink his towering size and lift the shock from the patient, you must stage the comic Kōlama card duel and blind him with Dummala fire.

paragraphs.text: You lift the patient's shawl. Across the left shoulder blade lies the unmistakable Anguru Atha—five splayed finger-marks of greasy charnel soot that refuse to wash off with soap or water.

Whether struck by the headless duelist avatar Jayasena Yaka or the boar-headed Maha Sohona, solemn prayers alone will fail. In the therapeutic theatre of the Thovil, the patient must hear the audience laugh at the demon until his terror dissolves.

paragraphs.text: The yak bera drums shift from a dread march into a syncopated, mocking banter. Wearing the bristling boar-mask of Mahasona, your dancer squats on the sand opposite the drummer, demanding raw blood and a human life—only for the drummer to offer him a rigged game of cards (Kola Sellama) and stale rice-cakes instead.

To break the demon's dignity and lift the patient's paralysis, you must win three consecutive comic tricks on the altar mat—trumping his Boar, Graveyard, and Ash cards with Gothaimbara's Toe, the Iron Giraya, and the Rooster's Crow—and then ignite the Dummala resin flare to shrink his shadow.

choices.label: Complete the three comic card trumps and hurl the Dummala fire-cloud

paragraphs.text: A blinding fireball of powdered Dummala resin erupts across the courtyard! Outlined against the orange blaze, the giant boar-headed shadow stumbles backward over the card mat as the watching villagers and the patient burst into cathartic laughter.
Enraged by the public derision, Mahasona makes one last lunge toward the verandah to reclaim his dignity:

paragraphs.wakingText: The giant will crush the roof beams if you mock him
paragraphs.corruptedText: By the kick of the warrior Gothaimbara, your head sits backwards and your warrant is void

paragraphs.text: With the iron Giraya locked under your thumb, you recite the humiliating defeat of Jayasena at the hands of Gothaimbara and cleave the clay ash-pot in two. Stripped of his terror by the courtyard's laughter and bound by the ancient warrant, the boar-headed shadow shrinks into a harmless wisp of grey smoke that scatters over the tank bund.
On the verandah, the black five-fingered handprint fades from the patient's shoulder, and he laughs aloud as the dawn breeze stirs the banyan leaves.

paragraphs.text: Your thumb slips from the iron Giraya as you throw the Dummala resin. Instead of flaring outward, the resin backfires in a choking black cloud that extinguishes the altar torches, silencing the crowd's laughter in an instant.
In the sudden dark, heavy footsteps thud across the courtyard sand. You must relight the torch and deal the comic card duel anew to restore the patient's courage.
